40% of Slovenia’s land is protected, the highest share among OECD countries.
 Slovenia also performs strongly in other environmental areas, such as recycling rates and overall water quality. 
 But challenges remain, particularly around biodiversity loss, reducing transport emissions and adapting to intensifying climate risks.
 Slovenia has set an ambitious goal of reaching net zero by 2045. Achieving it will require not only reducing emissions but also ensuring that investment, infrastructure and economic incentives support a greener and more resilient economy.
 Launched today, the second #OECD Environmental Performance Review of Slovenia looks at the progress made and the policies that can support the country's transition towards a sustainable and net-zero economy.

Our 2026–2027 Project Ready Student Leaders kicked off their first session with reflection, goal-setting, and a little friendly competition! 🎓✨

 Getting to Know the League: Students learned more about the Urban League of Greater Chattanooga (ULGC) and the National Urban League (NUL), exploring our history, mission, and the impact of our work in communities.

 From setting goals for the future to learning the power of their own community and putting their problem-solving skills to the test, our Student Leaders are already thinking bigger, building stronger, and preparing to lead.
 This is just the beginning! ❤️

items.content_text:
We’re proud to celebrate Cassie Davis, Hamilton County Schools’ Manager for Climate and Capacity Building, on her selection for Leadership Chattanooga’s 2026 cohort!

Selected as one of 45 community leaders, Cassie is spending the next 10 months learning alongside professionals from across Chattanooga as part of a leadership development experience focused this year on Growth-Minded Leadership.

The journey kicked off with a two-day retreat in Knoxville, where the cohort explored leadership styles, trust, collaboration and what it means to help create high-performing, high-learning cultures. But for Cassie, one of the most meaningful parts of the experience has been the relationships she’s already building with people from across the community.

“I expected to learn a lot about Chattanooga and leadership, but I didn't necessarily expect how quickly I would feel connected to this group of people,” Cassie shared. “I genuinely feel like we have the best class ever!”

As she continues the 10-month experience, Cassie hopes to bring what she learns back to Hamilton County Schools — strengthening connections across the community, finding new opportunities to collaborate and ultimately helping create better outcomes for students and families.

We’re excited to follow Cassie’s Leadership Chattanooga journey and see where these connections and conversations take her — and our community — over the next 10 months. 💙

🏠 An opportunity for two pieces of Chattanooga history.
 Two historic brick homes in the Park Place neighborhood are headed to auction, offering new owners the chance to breathe new life into a pair of Victorian-era houses in the heart of Chattanooga.
 Park Place is an important part of the historic fabric surrounding the MLK Boulevard corridor, and properties like these help give the neighborhood its distinctive character and sense of place.
 We hope their next chapter includes thoughtful rehabilitation and continued stewardship of the architectural features that have allowed these homes to remain part of Chattanooga’s story for generations.
 Historic houses don’t have to be frozen in time. With the right investment, they can be adapted for contemporary life while retaining the character that makes them irreplaceable.
 Read more in the article below. 👇
 https://www.chattanoogan.com/…/2-Historic-Brick-Park-Place-…
 #PreserveChattanooga #HistoricPreservation #ChattanoogaHistory

The challenges shaping Tennessee’s future are regional, and so are many of the solutions.

Members of our SETD team traveled to Nashville yesterday for the 2026 ThinkTennessee Policy Forum, joining leaders from across the state for conversations around workforce development, transportation, housing, energy and economic growth.

From navigating growth across Tennessee’s counties to strengthening the workforce pipeline and preparing for increasing energy demand, the day offered valuable perspectives on many of the same opportunities and challenges we see here in Southeast Tennessee.

Opportunities like this help us bring new ideas and statewide perspectives back to our work while continuing to bring thoughtful, collaborative approaches to building a stronger region.

Thank you to ThinkTennessee for bringing together voices from across Tennessee for an important day of conversation and collaboration!

items.content_text:
The #OECD headline inflation was broadly stable at 4.1% in July 2026, as energy inflation stabilised above 10%. Increases in headline inflation across 13 OECD countries were largely balanced by declines in 14, while rates remained broadly stable in 11.
 Year-on-year energy inflation within the OECD and core inflation (inflation excluding food and energy) were broadly stable at 11.6% and 3.6%, respectively, although energy inflation remained above 10% for the fourth consecutive month.
 Food inflation declined in 23 OECD countries in July, including falls of 2.0 percentage points (p.p.) or more in Greece, Hungary and Latvia. As a result, OECD food inflation fell to 3.2% in July, after 3.4% in June.
 Learn more:  https://brnw.ch/21x5AND
 #OECDstats

items.title: Commission Meeting Summary — September 8, 2026  Vacation & Comp Time Policies — The commission approved Resolution 579,...
items.content_text:
Commission Meeting Summary — September 8, 2026 
 Vacation & Comp Time Policies — The commission approved Resolution 579, updating the vacation accrual schedule for key management/department heads, aimed at helping the city stay competitive in attracting and retaining experienced leaders. Resolution 580 was also approved, removing the previous 5-year cap on compensatory time accrual for non-exempt hourly employees. 
 Flag Policy Adopted — After weeks of discussion sparked by local American Legion and VFW representatives, the commission approved Resolution 581, adopting a formal city-wide flag policy. The policy sets flag sizing based on flagpole height (the "one-quarter rule") and calls for a 20'x38' U.S. flag at Veterans Memorial Park's 125-ft pole — down from the current oversized flag, which veterans groups said posed a safety risk to handlers, was causing wear on the equipment, didn't conform to flag code, and hung too low at half-staff. Commissioner Howse requested preserving flexibility to fly a larger flag for special occasions; after the vote, City Manager Holmes noted that flexibility is already built in, since a future commission can authorize a larger flag via resolution. Several citizens also spoke against the change, noting the memorial flag has flown for around 22 years. 
 Courtroom Dedication — Commission approved Resolution 582, renaming the City Hall courtroom the "Judge Kevin B. Wilson Memorial Courtroom," honoring his 35 years on the bench (1990–2025). Judge Wilson passed away in January 2026. 
 Structural Cabling Bid — Commission approved awarding the City Hall cabling upgrade project to Ontivity, LLC, the lowest of five bids received (~$59,869), to replace outdated network/phone cabling. 
 Airport Advisory Board — From 12 applicants, the commission approved the top four vote-getters (Jack Farrow, John Record, Heath Merz, and Michael Brown), then broke a three-way tie for the fifth seat in favor of Zoe Krohne. Final appointments will be formalized by resolution at the September 21 meeting. 
 License Plate Reader (Flock) Contract — Following growing national concerns regarding use of LPR technology — and after a local law enforcement agency suspended its own use of the technology — the commission voted to withdraw from its contract with Flock Safety, following a formal recommendation from Collegedale Chief of Police and city administration. Police access to the cameras had already been revoked pending this discussion. 
 Withdrawal involves per-camera removal fees (~$500 each) offset by prorated fee refunds, with cameras to come down within a "reasonable timeframe" after written notice. Flock cameras are also used by private organizations and on private property. These are not regulated by the City of Collegedale or any other government entity, and the city has no right to remove them since they are not installed or controlled within city right-of-way. Public comment was largely opposed to the cameras, citing constitutional concerns and privacy worries. 
 Other Notes — Commission discussed finalizing a date for the Christmas Parade (leaning toward a survey to gauge community preference among Nov. 21, Nov. 28, or Dec. 5, and whether to pair it with the Christmas tree lighting). Staff is also pursuing CPR certification for employees and coordinating with the Health Department on a mobile vaccination van for tetanus shots. Brief updates were given on the playground project, railroad camera project, and right-of-way work on Little Debbie Parkway. 
 View the meeting recording here: https://www.collegedaletn.gov/…/agenda…/livestream/index.php

items.content_text:
Official Statement: Collegedale Police Department Discontinues Flock License Plate Reader (LPR) System
 COLLEGEDALE, TN (September 9, 2026) – The following statement was issued by Jack Sapp, Chief of Police, Collegedale Police Department:
 "On Thursday, September 3, 2026, I made the decision to discontinue access to the Flock License Plate Reader (LPR) system for all officers of the Collegedale Police Department, revoking access to the six (6) LPR cameras operated by the City. This decision followed careful consideration of the technology, its use, and concerns expressed by citizens of Collegedale, as well as individuals who travel through and visit our community.
 At the same time, access to Collegedale’s LPR cameras by outside agencies was also revoked.
 During the September 8, 2026, meeting of the Collegedale Board of Commissioners, I formally recommended that the City terminate all contracts and agreements with Flock for use of LPR technology. The Board of Commissioners voted unanimously to approve that recommendation.
 The Collegedale Police Department no longer utilizes or maintains access to Flock or any other LPR vendor systems, networks, or databases. While LPR technology has provided valuable assistance to our officers and investigators, the benefits of any law enforcement tool must be carefully weighed against the concerns, expectations, and the support of the citizens.
 The Collegedale Police Department remains committed to protecting public safety while also respecting the trust and concerns of the community we serve."
 This statement is being provided in lieu of individual interviews at this time.

What did tax reform look like last year?
 The 2026 edition of the OECD Tax Policy Reforms report tracks key developments across 92 jurisdictions. Here are five key findings that shaped tax policy in 2025:
 ➡️Tax policy continued to balance growth support with mounting budgetary pressures, although revenue-raising measures remained relatively limited.
 ➡️Personal income tax reforms increased progressivity, alongside targeted relief to support households and attract talent.
 ➡️Corporate tax rates remained broadly stable, with more use of targeted incentives and sector-specific taxes.
 ➡️VAT reforms advanced digitalisation, while health taxes were among the most common revenue-raising measures.

Space is becoming a critical part of our economies. How can governments support innovation and competitiveness in the space sector? 
 Commercial space activity is accelerating with 109 countries having put at least one satellite into orbit by 2025, more than double the number in 2014.
 This growing participation reflects an expanding space economy which is becoming essential to critical infrastructure such as transport, energy, communications and food supply. 
 Governments have a key role shaping the space economy. Public R&D, procurement, regulation, finance and support for commercialisation can help attract investment, foster innovation and strengthen competitive space ecosystems.
 The #OECD Space Economy at a Glance 2026 explores how governments can support the next wave of innovation and competitiveness while ensuring that space remains safe, sustainable and accessible.

HCSO Recovers Missing Person from Overturned Vehicle
 On the evening of September 6, HCSO deputies responded to a report of a missing person at the 1900 block of Aslinger Road.
 Family members of 79-year-old Lewis Faucet told deputies they believe Faucet could have experienced a medical emergency.
 HCSO detectives initiated a search, found Faucet’s vehicle overturned about a mile from his residence, and safely removed him from the vehicle. He was taken back to his residence, where he was turned over to medical personnel for further evaluation. 
 This information is preliminary and subject to change. No further details are available.

items.title: Fall on Signal Mountain is pretty hard to beat. 🍂 The leaves are starting to change, the temperatures are cooling down...
items.content_text:
Fall on Signal Mountain is pretty hard to beat. 🍂
 The leaves are starting to change, the temperatures are cooling down (ever so slowly,) and soon our beautiful trees will be putting on their annual show. Of course, that also means we get a LOT of leaves! 
 But before you reach for the leaf blower, let’s leave the leaves when we can.
 Fallen leaves:
 🦋 Provide winter shelter for butterflies, moths, fireflies and other wildlife
 🌱 Return nutrients to the soil
 🍂 Act as natural mulch
 🌿 Support a healthier ecosystem
 And there’s no need to rush. Wildlife needs those leaves throughout fall and winter. When you can, leave them where they fall, mulch them into your lawn, or move them into garden beds.
 BUT let's be smart about it.
 Near a storm drain? Move them. Leaves that wash into storm drains can cause drainage problems.
 In the street? Please don't blow them there. Leaf piles can create a one-lane situation for cars, bikes and pedestrians.
 🍁 Leaf pickup begins in October. Follow Signal Mountain Public Works for updates on pickup timing and zones.
 Want to learn more? Check out the National Wildlife Federation's Leave the Leaves campaign for more information and tips.
 Leave the leaves when you can. Move them when you need to.
 And when in doubt, reach out!

 It measures what students know and can do in science, reading, maths. For the first time, it also assesses how students learn and solve problems using digital tools.
 More than 760 000 students across 91 countries and economies took part, making it the largest PISA assessment to date.
 Which education systems performed best? And what does PISA reveal about students’ AI use and attitudes towards learning?
 OECD Director for Education and Skills, Andreas Schleicher explains⤵️

items.title: The latest #OECDPISA results, released today, show that student performance has declined across all three core subjects...
items.content_text:
The latest #OECDPISA results, released today, show that student performance has declined across all three core subjects over the past decade.
 Across OECD countries between 2015 and 2025:
 ➡️ Reading scores fell by 28 points, the steepest decline of the three subjects.
 ➡️ Mathematics scores dropped by 22 points, equivalent to just over one year of learning.
 ➡️ Science proved more resilient, with scores declining by 7 points.
 The results underline the importance of strengthening the knowledge and skills students need for the future. Strong foundations in reading, mathematics and science enable students to think, learn and use #AI effectively.
 Learn more about the results: https://brnw.ch/21x5wl9
